cohort: Women who had deliveries in the US between 2011 and 2014, with a subset identified as having beta-thalassemia major and matched to controls.
finding: Women with beta-thalassemia major are more likely to experience C-section delivery, require blood transfusions, and have neonates who are small for gestational age.
mod_finding: C-section was 30% more likely to be the method of birth among participants with beta-thalassemia major.
